query: configure a custom OpenAI-compatible API base URL, how the model list is fetched from /models, and per-conversation chat history
raw_response:
### API base URL configuration

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/tutorials/integrations/dev-tools/continue-dev

Points the extension to the Open WebUI API endpoint.

```yaml
apiBase: http://localhost:3000/api
```

--------------------------------

### Fetch Final Chat History

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/reference/api-flow

Retrieve the complete conversation history for a given `chatId` using a GET request to the chats endpoint.

```bash
curl -X GET https://<host>/api/v1/chats/<chatId> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
```

### vLLM

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/quick-start/connect-a-provider/starting-with-vllm

vLLM provides an OpenAI-compatible API (Chat Completions), which simplifies integration with Open WebUI. The default API base URL for a vLLM server is typically http://localhost:8000/v1.

--------------------------------

### Connect a model > Connection fields

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/ecosystem/computer/ai/connect-a-model

When configuring a connection, you must provide a Base URL and an API Key. For services like Ollama that do not require authentication, the API Key field must still contain non-empty text. Optional fields include a display name, a Prefix ID for namespacing model IDs, and a specific list of models to use.

--------------------------------

### Getting Started > Quick Start > Connect a Provider > Starting with OpenAI-Compatible > Required API Endpoints

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/quick-start/connect-a-provider/starting-with-openai-compatible

To ensure full compatibility with Open WebUI, servers should implement specific OpenAI-standard endpoints. The core chat functionality requires the /v1/chat/completions endpoint. Model discovery is facilitated by /v1/models, though models can be manually allowlisted if this endpoint is unavailable. Additional features like RAG, Text-to-Speech, Speech-to-Text, and Image Generation require their respective /v1/embeddings, /v1/audio/speech, /v1/audio/transcriptions, and /v1/images/generations endpoints.
